The sutta sets out the theme of practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma (*dhammānudhammapaṭipanna*) [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral identifies a substantial web of passage-level parallels across early Buddhist verse literature [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Canon, verse parallels are found in the Dhammapada (Dhp 364) and the Theragāthā (Thag 17.3, the *Ānandattheragāthā*) [SuttaCentral]. In non-Pali corpora, parallels occur widely in the Dharmapada and Udānavarga traditions: the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 51–90, *Bhikhuvagga*), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 216–238, *Śaraṇavagga*), Sanskrit recensions of the Udānavarga (UV 32 and UVS 32, *Bhikṣuvarga*), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 32), and three Chinese Dharmapada/Udānavarga translations (T 210.34, T 212.33, and T 213.32) [SuttaCentral]. Another narrative parallel is attested in the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu* (San Lo Mvu 107, *The Jātaka of Asthisena*) [SuttaCentral].
